title: OpenAI Responses v15: toolcall handshake + streaming fragmentation resilience
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Add compatibility shims and resilient reassembly logic for the OpenAI Responses v15 streaming shape. This PR improves tool/function-call handshake semantics, preserves determinism/seed hints across fragmented stream frames, and implements a fragmentation-resilient reassembly layer so that large structured outputs and tool call payloads are robustly reconstructed even under partial retransmits or chunk reordering. Motivation: customers running structured tool-calling workloads observed missing tool arguments or truncated JSON objects when gateway/network proxies produced out-of-order frames or when the streaming adapter split tokens mid-JSON attribute. v15 of the OpenAI Responses shape introduces a few new metadata flags (seed_hint, rng_hint, response_annotations) which we need to forward without mutation; it also allows tool-call frames to arrive interleaved with assistant delta frames. This work prevents silent data loss and preserves deterministic seeds passed from upstream.

What changed (high-level): - Introduced a StreamFrameSequence reassembler in the openai-adapter that tracks per-stream fragment ids and assembly windows; supports idempotent reassembly on duplicate fragments. - Added a toolcall handshake protocol: HEAD/ACK pair encoded as small control frames so receiver can atomically mark tool invocation boundaries before parsing. - Propagate seed_hint and rng_hint verbatim from incoming v15 frames to Redwood Responses internal envelope and to log traces. - Preserve annotations and metadata_passthrough map; added tests and logging around annotation collisions. - Added a compatibility shim for older downstream clients: if a downstream sends a legacy toolcall frame we synthesize v15-compatible control frames to avoid parsing errors. - Observability: new trace spans for reassembly time and a labeled metric for fragmented messages reassembled_count.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-5123) - [x] Unit tests for reassembler and handshake - [x] Integration test: chunk-reorder + duplicate-fragment scenarios - [x] E2E test against openai-bridge fixture v15 - [x] Backward-compatible: falls back to previous behavior when fragmentation not detected - [x] Release notes entry - [x] Ops rollout plan added

Commit summary: - a1b3c2e: add StreamFrameSequence reassembler + unit tests - d4f7b8a: implement toolcall HEAD/ACK control frames and parsing hooks - e9f0a12: pass-through seed_hint/rng_hint and wire annotations; update tracing - f2c3d45: integration tests for reordered/duplicated fragments - 9b1a7fd: docs and release-notes; minor lint fixes

Files changed (high-level): - openai-adapter/stream/reassembler.py (new) - openai-adapter/stream/handshake.py (new) - openai-adapter/handlers.py (modifications to parsing/dispatch) - responses-proxy/compat/shims_v15.py (compat shim for legacy toolcalls) - telemetry/tracing.py (new spans) - tests/integration/test_stream_fragmentation.py - docs/compat/openai_v15.md (compatibility notes)

Review conversation (highlights): - Diego Rivera (reviewer): "Nice isolation of reassembly logic. Two nits: rename get_window -> current_window; add an assertion on fragment sequence monotonicity." - Author (Aisha): "Renamed and added assertion; assertion guarded behind debug flag to avoid perf impact in prod." - Mei Chen (reviewer): "Concern: head/ack control frames increase control surface — how do we avoid DOS by sending many small HEAD frames?" - Author: "Handshake includes a per-connection rate limit; we treat excessive HEAD frames as malformed and metric it. Added tests.`" - Lucas Ortega (approver): "Integration tests caught an edge-case with duplicate fragments; LGTM after addressing the post-merge follow-up for improved metrics labels." - Ops (comment): "Needs a slow rollout — fragmentation edge cases correlate with older LB versions; will coordinate canary on Dedicated clusters."

CI / Checks: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests: pass - lint: pass (one auto-fix) - benchmark-smoke: pass - security-scan: pass

Merge outcome: Squash merged to main (merge commit: squash/72645-openai-v15-toolcall-frag-resilience). Merged by Lucas Ortega on 2026-02-22.

Deployment & Rollout: - Canary rollout to 5% of Hosted region-us-east first, monitor reassembled_count and toolcall_error_rate. - If reassembled_count increases above baseline (expected during canary), validate that toolcall success rate increases and deterministic seeds are present in traces. - Ops will pause and rollback if toolcall_error_rate rises > 2x baseline for 10m.

Backward compatibility notes: - Default behavior unchanged for non-fragmented streams. - Legacy toolcall frames are auto-upgraded by the shim to avoid client changes. - The seed_hint and rng_hint are forwarded but not interpreted by Redwood runtime; they are available to eval/trace tooling.

Follow-ups (tracked as Linear): - ENG-5180: Add structured-output schema validator for reassembled payloads - ENG-5234: Expose reassembly diagnostics in Console per-route tab - ENG-5299: Hardening for very large multi-MB toolcall payloads (chunking policies)

Release notes: Adds v15 OpenAI Responses compatibility: robust streaming reassembly, improved tool/function-call handshake, and metadata passthrough for seed/rng hints. This reduces truncated toolcall payloads and preserves determinism annotations across the gateway.
release_notes: v15 compatibility: reassembly + toolcall handshake + seed/rng passthrough (see docs/compat/openai_v15.md)
